kicker: A brain in a jar can only talk. Give it hands, and it starts doing.

jar.label: Brain in a jar
jar.art: Dawn over a sand garden. A brain in a glass jar only lets out bubbles of words. Around the jar, on flat stones: a browser, files, a calendar and an inbox, all out of reach.
jar.before: Chatbot without tools: answers in words only
jar.done: Four ink strokes reach out: open the browser, fetch a file, circle a meeting, send an email.
jar.insight: Without tools, a chatbot only answers in words. An agent is an AI model with tools, so it gets work done.
jar.detail: Instead of telling you how to open the calendar, an agent opens it, finds a free slot, books the meeting. Many chat apps now have some tools built in.

anatomy.label: Anatomy of an agent
anatomy.art: A diagram of an agent in the garden: a brain seated at a desk, four ink arms holding tools, two lanterns, a scroll of plans and a fence.

parts.name: Brain
parts.text: Reads the situation, thinks, then decides the next step.

parts.name: Hands
parts.text: Searches the web, reads files, sends emails, clicks buttons… to actually do things, not just talk.

parts.name: Paper lantern
parts.text: Whatever is in this conversation. When the job is done, the lantern goes out.

parts.name: Stone lantern
parts.text: Saved notes and files; next time, the agent opens them and picks up where it left off.

parts.name: Scroll
parts.text: Breaks a big goal into small steps, does them in order, ticks each one off.

parts.name: Desk
parts.text: Where the agent gets to work: a computer, a browser, file folders.

parts.name: Fence
parts.text: Permissions: it only does what is allowed. Confirmation: big actions must ask you first.

anatomy.insight: An agent has a brain, hands, memory and a plan, all working inside a safety fence.
anatomy.detail: Without a fence, an agent can get big things wrong. Give it just enough access, and make it ask before sending, deleting or paying.

loop.label: The agent loop
loop.art: A ring of stones on raked sand. In the middle: the goal and the report. Around the ring, four stones: plan, act, check the result, self-correct.

steps.text: Book a team meeting on Friday that all 5 people can attend.
Break it down: check each calendar, pick a time, and only then send invites.
Open the calendar, try holding 9:00 on Friday morning.
The calendar says: An is busy at 9:00. Goal not met yet.
Drop 9:00. Need a time when all 5 people are free.
New plan: try 14:00 on Friday afternoon.
Hold 14:00 on Friday in the calendar.
All 5 people are free at 14:00. Goal met.
Report back: 14:00 is on hold. Invites go out only once you agree.

insight.text: An agent works in a loop: plan, act, check the result, self-correct — repeat until done, then report.

loop.detail: Tip for handing off work: state the goal clearly, what “done” looks like, and what the agent must ask you first.

quiz.q: What turns a chatbot into an agent?
options: Tools to do the work itself
quiz.explain: An agent is an AI model with tools, a plan and a self-correcting loop, so it gets things done, not just talks.

summary: An agent is an AI brain with hands: it acts, checks the result, fixes itself, then reports.

anthropic-agents-2024.title: Building effective agents
anthropic-agents-2024.note: Describes agents as language models that use tools on their own, guided by feedback from their environment, running in a loop.
